I went into this game completely blind. The only reason why I decided to choose this game among all of the otome games on steam was because of a recommendation on an online forum. SO GLAD I decided to listen to that rec! 
The only experience I had with Cheritz before this was with Mystic Messenger. I really liked that game, but ultimately had to drop it because of the real time gameplay elements. Since this game is a regular visual novel, I was finally able to enjoy another beautiful story told by the Cheritz team stress free!!
All of the characters are just so silly and charming! Even though I only have a crush on Red and Yujin, I absolutely LOVE all of the other characters. (Even the side characters!) I REALLY liked the plot of this game, but it’s so important (for me) to have fully fleshed out characters in my visual novels, and Cheritz totally delivered on that! 
Speaking about the plot, I really like the concept of a lonely grieving learning how to live and love again is so compelling. Seeing how she approaches relationships differently than other MCs due to her sadness (and shame from her hobbies) makes a much more compelling and relatable MC compared to other otome games. Even though her grief is an important part of the plot, the story mainly focuses on a slice of life/school scenario. I really like simple slice of life stories, so it didn’t bother me. 
Overall, if you enjoy goofy characters and antics with emotional plot points, I think this would be a good game to play. Please keep in mind that this game does contain triggering content!

O começo da história é um tiquinho arrastado, cheguei até a parar depois da intro para jogar outro date sim e deixei o jogo de lado por umas semanas. Mas depois de voltar ao hype de Mystic Messenger resolvi voltar com Nameless e, nossa, como vale a pena. A história é bem construída, de forma que você fica gradualmente mais interessada na história principal.

Esse jogo foi um caso raro em que não acertei de cara quem seriam meus favoritos. Fiquei apaixonada pelo Lance, o "príncipe gélido", a personalidade dele é desenvolvida muito bem, ainda mais para uma Rota Casual. Ele é de longe meu favorito. No entanto, a história do Red foi minha segunda favorita e olha que eu tava achando ele um saco no início do jogo. Aprofundaram bem os sentimentos dele e o arco emocional dele é um dos mais amarradinhos.

O jogo tem sim alguns personagens mais problemáticos (cofcof Tei // cofcof Yeonho na rota dele mesmo) e acho que a história poderia envolver mais escolhas e agência para a player, mas considerando o ano de produção, acho que não foge muito dos padrões que se esperaria de outras produções de 2013.

Enfim, a dinâmica dos personagens entre si é muito divertida e gosto de como a amizade deles nas rotas diferentes ainda são genuínas e fofas com a MC. Recomendo :)

There is a lot I can say about this game, but the biggest thing is that the stories have stayed with me for all these years. This is one of the best otome games that I have played. Each story line is gripping yet heart breaking. Sometimes, even the good ends feel like bad ends. You are constantly yearning for everything to get better and feeling absolutely down trodden when it doesn't. I had to stop playing this game numerous times because of how emotionally impactful it was. Even characters I wasn't too fond of in the main route I grew to adore them towards the end. Yuri ended up becoming one of my favorite character because of how they handled his route alone.
The pacing of the story matches the life for the MC they are trying to show and I will admit, it feels like a real slow burn. But, it is worth it. 
The true route is worth all of the angst the prior routes provided and the bad endings demonstrated the depths of each character more so.  It reminded me of Amnesia: Memories with how integral the bad ends were to fully understanding the character route I chose to follow.

I played this game many years ago, but I still think about it to this day. This is a game I recommend to any of my friends looking for an intense story. My gaming library is filled with games just like this one, but none of them has touched me in the way this one did. I just don't have the heart to reset my save file to play again. It feels like I'd be erasing all of their progress if I did.

What a ride. I had this VN in my backlog for a long time, as I thought I wasn't ready for something mushy or naive. I was incredibly wrong, the theme of this game is mature and the routes are interesting and varied. Note that I'm quite picky haha.

The MC is fantastic, she has a lot of character and she's not completely helpless, she explores growing up, friendships and relationships. A few times, I laughed or I gulped, as the story is pretty enthralling despite the art style not necessarily being my jam. When I wasn't playing the game due to life happening, I couldn't wait for free time to play it.

I feel like this game and its counterpart, Dandelion - Wishes brought to you, are fantastic and different from the general otoges because these are Korean games, so they don't shy away from MC with great character, mature stories and overall the treatment of the LI are clearly different from the usual knight in shining armor and fair maiden often shown in Japanese media (although it is starting to change).

For a few cons, there are quite a bit of typos in the English version, it is clear that the people who translated it didn't have access to the game itself; a character with green hair and eyes is translated as having blue hair, as it is generally the same name for both colors. The CG didn't always wow me and the art style wasn't necessarily my thing but you easily forget about as the story is really great.

It's a must play for anyone who likes maiden games!

I really enjoyed this visual novel. It probably sits in my top five visual novels I have played. At the very least in the top ten. And I have played a couple dozen by this point. 

I didn't expect it to tug at the heart strings as it did. Other times it could be shocking or disturbing, intentionally so, some of the bad endings. Overall adorable and charming with compelling characters. This is one of those visual novels that truly makes me think, "wow, I would have loved reading this as a manga or watching as a anime" because of the writing. 

And I will second it, indie developers are the ones to support with buying visual novels in my opinion. Big companies stick to a formula when they create visual novels. "Why fix what isn't broke," seems to be their motto. Why spend more money on innovating visual novels they create, when it just opens them up to risk and a greater loss of profits. 

Indie developers are the ones pushing expanding upon what visual novels are. They innovate. They ask themselves what they would want in a visual novel and consider what others are looking for as they develop visual novels. My favorite visual novels I have played have all been made by indie developers. 

I have played some good visual novels made by big companies, but typically after I have played through each route character's route once, there really is no draw to ever play the game again. Being highly replayable isn't something big companies really want their visual novels to be. Since the main thing visual novels of big companies give me is a new story to get lost in for a bit. Along with some beautiful art. But they tend to come with a higher price sticker.

Okay, so firstly a confession. 
I play these sorts of games with friends for the laugh factor. Who doesn't like a hefty dose of over the top drama after all? 
And generally, these games are perfect giant blocks of Limburgur, being so ridiculously full of cheese. 

I'm not saying this wasn't, but oh my gosh. 
We just kept coming back for more. 

Having played Dandelion, the hint of a story line beyond the surface of what we saw, shocked us (thank you early on bad ending that we stumbled into like a very messed up Narnia). This meant that the curiosity seed had been planted, and you can bet we needed to figure out what the heck was going on. 

22 hours later. . . . here we are.  
(Organizing playtime is hard for a group. And sometimes we'd be our own voice actors. Let me tell you it's a very different story if you do it that way. The Voice actors they have do an amazing Job, and really help sell the story. My falsetto. . . not so much.) 

There are fun twists, some as obvious as the sun that do be shining (but like the sun we tend to ignore it unless we're forced to look right at it) and also some really lovely character development. Which was both surprising, and quite lovely. There are definitely routes that stood head and shoulders above others, but that also could just be personal opinion. 

I don't know your taste. 
But some really do live up to the principal of a quote I saw once:
"It's easier to notice the green flag when it's standing in a field of red ones."

But the good dudes are genuinely so wholesome. Mad support for those dudes. 

And then the bad endings. . . 
Traumatizing. Made our skin crawl. Feeling yourself curl into as close an approximation of a pretzel that a human body can be, while being aware that your friends are doing exactly the same so great is the force of recoil, honestly a very bonding moment. 10/10 would recommend.

The only real letdown was the end. 
It felt like it was built up to something a bit bigger, and there was little attatchment to how it panned out. But Still I have no regrets about spending clse to a day (dear lord) playing this. It was great fun.

Overall, I think it's a 8/10, because the secret character/ending, ended very suddenly, and closure would've been appreciated. Still a great game. Tei is the best :)

i wish steams recommendation system wasnt just "yes" or "no" because im honestly pretty mixed on this game.

[b]PROS[/b]
[*]ive only finished i think 2 routes so far and ive already clocked 17 hours in the game- theres i think 6 routes total, so the amount of gameplay available is insane
[*]contains what is probably one of the most positive and realistic portrayals of teenage girls friendship, like i love it so so much, the friendship between mc and her 2 school friends is fantastic and i wish i saw even more of it
[*]cheritz is pretty good at making each route unique despite them all taking place in what is technically the same storyline
[*]has i think 2 minigames you play in most routes that are pretty fun! the quiz needs to be aced to get good endings and it can be HARD and stressful but i enjoyed that! it felt like a real test lol
[*]USUALLY the mc has her head on her shoulders and actually has a personality along with hobbies and interests. she stands up for herself frequently without being too "im girlboss hear me roar" unrealistic. i more often than not was rooting for and empathizing with her struggles and concerns. [/list]

however i think thats kind of where the pros stop for me. the cons  are... well....

[b]CONS[/b]
[*]the game is definitely a product of its time and pretty much everything shows it. the ui is pretty outdated, low quality graphically, and i didn't even know you could open a menu full of additional functions until my second route. 
[*]mc is in high school and one of her love interests is a grown man who sexually harasses her and is literally her teacher. they point it out in his route, too, that it's weird and kind of illegal but the game is like lol who cares???? ME. I CARE. IT'S WEIRD.
[*]the art is reallllly hit or miss- and it's mostly miss. the art style itself is fine because it's a unique style, but anatomy is often wack and theres massive color discrepancies between cgs- seriously, is mcs hair purple? brown? brurple? it changes vastly
[*]most of these character archetypes have aged very poorly. like okay we got the p3doph!le teacher preying on the kid he lives with, the insane teacher who threatens and attempts to kill students, the 2 innocent-on-the-outside characters who are so deluded by "love" for the mc that theyre okay with killing her if necessary. it's weird and hard to get through, honestly
[*]game costs $30 and when on sale it doesnt go down by very much
[*]youre probably going to need a guide to get good endings, one wrong choice will just screw your route entirely IF you can even get onto one in the first place.[/list]

so ill say "yes" to recommend because i like cheritz (and this game is very old) and i don't necessarily hate the game, but i wouldn't actually recommend it because for me the heavy cons are not worth dealing with for the occasional pro, especially for $30. but if you personally can get it on sale and look past the really outdated parts, you might enjoy it! i still has charm and it's kind of fun to see how this game definitely was a foundation that cheritz took a lot from when making the game theyre most known for, mystic messenger. and i liked seeing what they'd improved on between this game and mm. 

[u]tldr:[/u] if you really like cheritz or are used to the cultural and social culture around old visual novel games, you might like this one! otherwise: give it a pass, and watch a playthrough/read a description of the routes instead
